voices.1: en-US-AvaMultilingualNeural (chosen voice), base rate -8%, directed per passage (render_edge.py)

tracks.room: Street level · Calle Imagen entrance (or the north entrance)
tracks.title: Welcome to the Setas de Sevilla
tracks.where: At street level on the Plaza de la Encarnación, by the Calle Imagen entrance, near the escalators and the ramp that leads down to level minus one; stand to one side, out of the flow of people. If you arrive by the north entrance, from Calle Regina and José Gestoso, play it there before you go down.
tracks.what: Metropol Parasol, known as las Setas, by Jürgen Mayer H. (J. MAYER H., Berlin), engineered by Arup, opened 27 March 2011. The four layers: the Antiquarium on level −1, the Mercado de la Encarnación at street level, the Plaza Mayor raised square, the walkways and the Mirador 360º on top. The route, the three lengths of this guide, the Antiquarium's separate entry, access.
tracks.listen: What the Setas are, the four layers you will pass through from bottom to top to middle, and how the three lengths of this guide work.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — Found under a car park
tracks.where: On level minus one, at the entrance to the Antiquarium beside the taquilla, or on the first stretch of walkway inside, where the excavated remains first come into view.
tracks.what: The Antiquarium, the archaeological museum under the Setas, opened 27 March 2011; about 4,879 m² of excavated remains from the 1st century AD to the 13th century: Roman houses with mosaics, a Moorish (Almohad) house; remains of a 1st-century Roman fish-salting works also found on the site.
tracks.listen: How a plan for an underground car park turned into Seville's most important surviving Roman site.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — Seville stacked up
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, on the walkway at the first place where you can look down into the excavation and see how deep the remains go.
tracks.what: The 1991–92 test dig on the site of the old Mercado de la Encarnación (Verdugo Santos, Larrey Hoyuelos and Murillo Díaz, commissioned by the market traders' cooperative): convent remains, an Almohad level about 3 m down, a late-1st-century Roman building about 7 m down, Roman deposits to about 9 m; groundwater and a shored pit; the Setas designed as "a structure that sits on the Roman ruins".
tracks.listen: How a small test pit paid for by the market traders showed that every age of Seville lay stacked under this square.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — The House of the Column and its Medusa
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, among the Roman houses, at the label for the Casa de la Columna, the House of the Column, with its Medusa mosaic.
tracks.what: Roman Hispalis under the Plaza de la Encarnación: houses with mosaics built and rebuilt in several phases from the 1st century AD; the Casa de la Columna with its Medusa mosaic; in passing, the Casa Romana, Casa de las Basas, Casa del Sigma and Casa de la Noria; originals and replicas.
tracks.listen: Why this is Seville's best group of Roman mosaics, and the house of the Medusa.

tracks.room: Level −1 · Antiquarium, walking through the Roman houses
tracks.title: Antiquarium — Bacchus, the Nymph and the Ocean
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, heard while walking on through the Roman houses after the House of the Column. There is no fixed spot: play it as you go and read the labels. It names what to look for, never where it is.
tracks.what: The Casa de Baco, the Casa de la Ninfa, the Patio del Océano with a three-metre mural, and the Hospitium de los Delfines, as named by Seville city tourism, given as names to look for on the labels, with glosses; Roman houses rebuilt in phases into late antiquity. POSITION-FREE WALK-ALONG (lead decision 30 Oct 2026, after the V5 audit): it never says where any of them is. Check every name against the O4 label photos before release; if the labels aren't there, fold into 004 (ALT-A).
tracks.listen: Four Roman names to look for on the labels as you walk, what the names mean, and how the Roman city kept changing until the Moorish layer.

tracks.title: Antiquarium — The Almohad house
tracks.where: Inside the Antiquarium, at the label for the casa almohade, the Almohad house, the Moorish part of the excavation.
tracks.what: An Islamic house of the Almohad period, 12th–13th centuries, with traces of the surrounding Almohad neighbourhood; found about 3 m below the street in the 1991–92 test dig, against about 7 m for the Roman level. Context: the Almohad Great Mosque of Seville (ordered 1172) and its minaret, begun 1184, today's Giralda.
tracks.listen: How a house from Almohad Seville sits a thousand years and only a few metres above the Roman city, in the age of the Giralda.

tracks.title: Plaza de la Encarnación — A plaza with many lives
tracks.where: On level minus one, by the lifts that go up to the Mirador, beside the Antiquarium entrance. Play it while you wait; there is nothing you need to look at.
tracks.what: The Plaza de la Encarnación before the Setas: the Convento de la Encarnación (founded 1591), demolished under the Napoleonic decree of 1810; a wooden market by 1820; Melchor Cano's permanent market hall, built in the 1830s; the cut of 1948; demolition in 1973; the surface car park; the 1990s underground car-park plan that ran into Roman Seville.
tracks.listen: How one gap in the city, cleared by Napoleon's brother, was filled by a market, cars, archaeologists and finally the Setas.

tracks.title: Setas — Mushrooms of wood
tracks.where: Start it in the lift as the doors close; the second half plays as you step out onto the first stretch of walkway, among the timber of the parasols. Keep moving with the flow and stop at the rail only where you're out of the way.
tracks.what: Metropol Parasol by J. MAYER H. (Jürgen Mayer H.), winner of the 2004 international competition (65 entries); engineered with Arup; Kerto laminated veneer lumber made in Finland, about 3,400 elements made at Aichach near Munich, 2–3 mm polyurethane coating; concrete trunks with the lifts; the "largest wooden structure" claim and what the engineers say.
tracks.listen: How a competition, a nickname nobody planned and thousands of pieces of Finnish wood made the Setas.

tracks.room: Walkway · south side (where the Giralda is in clear view)
tracks.title: Walkway — The Cathedral and the Giralda
tracks.where: Anywhere on the walkway, or at the Mirador, where the Giralda, the cathedral's tall tower, and the cathedral beside it are in clear view above the rooftops. Stop at the rail where you're out of the way.
tracks.what: The Giralda: minaret of the Almohad Great Mosque, begun 1184, the cathedral's bell tower since the conquest of 1248, about 97.5 m to the top of the weathervane. Seville Cathedral: new church decided in 1401; called by UNESCO the largest Gothic building in Europe; World Heritage with the Alcázar and the Archivo de Indias. Link to the Setas: the cathedral's vaulting as a design cue; MoMA's 1:200 model (2004–07) and its "cathedral without walls".
tracks.listen: The tower and the church that gave the Setas one of its first ideas, seen across the rooftops.

tracks.room: Walkway · west side (the Giralda on your left)
tracks.title: Walkway — The river and the Aljarafe
tracks.where: On the walkway, at a spot on the rail where the Giralda, the cathedral's tall tower, is on your left: you are then facing west, toward the river. Stand close to the rail so others can pass.
tracks.what: The view west toward the Guadalquivir and the Aljarafe, the high ground west of the city; Roman Hispalis as a river port (D. González Acuña, "Hispalis, puerto romano de la Bética", 2010); the first-century fish-salting works excavated under the Plaza de la Encarnación (corridor paved with small bricks, five tanks about 3 m square, four of them excavated, filled on abandonment with rubbish, mostly compacted fish remains, out of use c. 70–120 AD). Not on view from here.
tracks.listen: Why the river made Roman Seville a port, and the Roman fish-salting tanks found under this square.

tracks.title: Walkway — The glue that had to be baked
tracks.where: Anywhere on the walkway on the way to the steps up to the Mirador, walking slowly or stopped at the rail out of the way of others, with the timber panels of the parasols around you.
tracks.what: The timber structure of the Setas: Kerto laminated veneer lumber panels by Finnforest, engineered by Arup; more than 3,000 joints with glued-in steel bars, about 35,000 holes drilled; the Fraunhofer WKI heat study and the tempering of the glued parts; the 2007 redesign; the largest panel 16.5 m tall.
tracks.listen: How thousands of glued joints were made to survive the Seville sun, and why the structure had to be re-engineered.

tracks.title: Mirador 360º — The highest point
tracks.where: At the top of the steps, on the Mirador 360º, the highest platform of the Setas. Find a place at the rail where you are not blocking the steps.
tracks.what: The Mirador 360º, the highest point of Metropol Parasol (J. Mayer H., 2004–2011): close to 30 m high, about 150 × 70 m, six parasols, a walkway about 250 m long; orientation to the Giralda and cathedral to the south and toward the river and the Aljarafe to the west.
tracks.listen: How high you are, the two sure landmarks to find, and the whole building stacked up beneath you.

tracks.title: Walkway — Love it or hate it
tracks.where: On the walkway after you come back down from the Mirador, heading toward the way down; walking, or stopped at the rail out of the way of others.
tracks.what: The controversy over Metropol Parasol: protests at the opening on 27 March 2011, the critics' verdict "como a un Cristo dos pistolas", Rowan Moore's review as relayed by Dezeen, Mayor Alfredo Sánchez Monteseirín's "moderna catedral urbana"; the four-year delay and the cost the city reported to Spain's Ombudsman, without the museum figure; Red Dot "Best of the Best" 2012, Mies van der Rohe Award finalist 2013, over a million visitors in the first year by one count.
tracks.listen: Why Seville argued about the Setas for years, what it cost, and what it won.

tracks.title: Walkway · Extra · Aurora, the Setas after dark
tracks.where: Anywhere on the walkway or at the Mirador, by day or after dark; stop at the rail out of the way of others.
tracks.what: Metropol Parasol Aurora (2021, for the tenth anniversary): a light and sound installation built into the timber; concept and software by Skandal Technologien; responds to visitor numbers and movement, weather, wind and season, with special programmes for days such as Semana Santa and the Feria; under 30% of the lights on at once.
tracks.listen: The light show built into the timber, and how it reacts to the crowd, the weather and the calendar.

tracks.room: Feeling Sevilla · before you go in
tracks.title: Feeling Sevilla · Extra · The room at 21 metres
tracks.where: Outside the entrance to the Feeling Sevilla room, the Sala Feeling, before you go in; follow the signs for Feeling Sevilla and stand aside from the door.
tracks.what: Sala Feeling, the multisensory room of Feeling Sevilla (Sacyr, 2021): about 21 m above the ground, over 200 m², curved LED screen 21 × 3 m, 360º sound, floor projection, LED ceiling lighting, air and scent effects; film about 15 minutes. The level inside the parasols in the architects' plan, on a steel-and-concrete platform.
tracks.listen: What the film room is, how it was added in 2021, and why not everything up here is wood.

tracks.title: The way down — From building site to city symbol
tracks.where: On the way down from the walkways to the Plaza Mayor, where the exhibition on the history of the Plaza de la Encarnación lines the route; play it as you walk down.
tracks.what: The official exhibition on the way down, showing the evolution of the Plaza de la Encarnación up to today (contents not yet photographed); building the Setas from June 2005; the opening on Sunday 27 March 2011 by Mayor Alfredo Sánchez Monteseirín, the Antiquarium the same evening; Arup's project director José de la Peña; Sacyr's concession and the 2021 renewal; DATED: 15th anniversary in 2026.
tracks.listen: How a building site Seville argued over became a city symbol, as you walk down past the exhibition.

tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — The market that waited 37 years
tracks.where: On the Plaza Mayor, the big raised square under the parasols; find a quiet spot away from the way down. The market is directly beneath this square, at street level.
tracks.what: The Mercado de la Encarnación: Melchor Cano's market hall of the 1830s, demolished 1973; temporary stalls for three years that lasted 37; the new market at street level under the Plaza Mayor, reopened 19 Dec 2010; fishmongers and greengrocers today.
tracks.listen: How the market's "temporary" move lasted 37 years, and how it came back under your feet.

tracks.title: Plaza Mayor — The plaza on stilts, and the way out
tracks.where: On the Plaza Mayor, the big raised square on the roof of the market, under the parasols; stand anywhere out of the way, ideally where you can see the parasols overhead.
tracks.what: The Plaza Mayor of Metropol Parasol (J. Mayer H., opened 2011): the raised public square over the Mercado de la Encarnación, open to the sky and used for events; the 2011 indignados (15-M) protests and camp here; finalist, European Prize for Urban Public Space 2012; Mayer's "urban, democratic, open cathedral"; Aurora after sunset; the way out to the street.
tracks.listen: Why the raised square is the heart of the design, how protesters made it theirs in its first weeks, and how to leave.
